item.title: Branch Art Exhibit: Interventions in Our Landscape by Karen Sekikawa and Stephanie Calvet — Wed Sep 2, 12:00 AM — North York Central Library
item.description: Throughout the month of September, Interventions in our Landscape by artists Karen Sekikawa and Stephanie Calvet is on display at North York Central Library branch. Karen Sekikawa and Stephanie Calvet work at the intersection of architecture, photography, and design. Trained as architects and based in Toronto, they share a deep appreciation for culture and the built environment, often exploring neighbourhoods both locally and abroad. Their individual creative practices enrich their photography—Karen draws on her Japanese heritage through ikebana (flower arrangement), while Stephanie reconnects with design through urban sketching in pen and ink. Karen Sekikawa and Stephanie Calvet draw inspiration from architecture, street life, and built elements within the landscape. Their architectural background is reflected in their photography, which emphasizes form, texture, pattern, light and shadow. item.title: Fabric IQ y Ontología MCP: la capa semántica que entiende tu negocio — Fri Sep 4, 11:00 AM
item.description:
Microsoft Reactor Toronto La sesión final lleva la serie al nivel más avanzado: la semántica empresarial como fundamento de todos los agentes.
Fabric IQ (GA desde Build 2026) es la capa de contexto compartido que unifica Data Agents, modelos semánticos y Ontologías sobre OneLake.
Aprenderás qué es una Ontología en Fabric, cómo define entidades, relaciones, propiedades y reglas de negocio vinculadas a datos en vivo, y cómo exponerla como servidor MCP para que cualquier agente externo — Claude, Copilot, agentes de Foundry — pueda fundamentar su razonamiento en ella sin reescribir integraciones.
Construiremos un flujo multi-agente completo donde el orquestador consulta la Ontología vía MCP para entender el negocio, delega al Data Agent para los datos, y entrega respuestas consistentes y gobernadas.
Cerraremos con una hoja de ruta práctica: qué está GA, qué está en Preview, y cómo planificar la adopción en tu organización hoy mismo. Los últimos 15 minutos serán Q&A abierto.

item.description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years! ### 🌿 North Humber River Walk – 6th Annual! 🌿
We’re back for our **sixth year in a row** with this incredible walk — and it has become a true fan favourite! The North Humber River trail is one of Toronto’s most peaceful and nature-filled walks. It’s a longer walk, but that’s part of what makes it so rewarding.
You’ll get out of the city, follow the river, explore beautiful natural areas, and see just how far you can go when you give yourself the chance.
This walk is about challenging yourself just a little — you'd be surprised how far you can go! If you don't want to complete the entire walk, that's totally okay. You can leave along the way, and I can help you find the nearest way back toward public transit. We'll finish with a quick stop at Tim Hortons before heading back toward Kipling Station.

item.description:
[at Ben McNally Books] Join us at Ben McNally Books, in partnership with Freehand Books, to celebrate the launch of The Cartel and Other Cover Stories by Wayne Grady. Order a copy of The Cartel here. About the Book From bestselling novelist Wayne Grady comes the delightful and inventive The Cartel and Other Cover Stories , his first collection of short fiction. Just as cover songs are both tributes to other musicians and original works in themselves, here Grady masterfully reimagines classic short stories in a way that honours the originals while creating something entirely new.
Each story in this collection takes its inspiration from works by international masters of the form, including Anton Chekhov, Franz Kafka, and Lydia Davis, drawing together new contexts and connections. item.title: Movie Matinee: Some Like It Hot (1959) — Fri Sep 11, 2:00 PM — Forest Hill
item.description:
Join us for an afternoon screening of the 1959 classic Some Like It Hot ! “Billy Wilder’s zany cross-dressing comedy begins with a massacre – resembling the gangland St Valentine’s Day killings of 1929 – and ends with one of the most celebrated last lines in cinema history. Written in cahoots with the director’s new collaborator I.A.L. Diamond, Some Like It Hot ascends to inspired heights of silliness in-between, with Tony Curtis and Jack Lemmon both on career-best form as dragged-up musicians hiding out with Sugar Kane’s girl band. Both the gangster story and the screwball antics hark back to Hollywood films of the 1930s, but Wilder’s outrageous and subversive play with gender was truly boundary pushing and helped lead to a loosening of censorship after United Artists released the film without certification.” – British Film Institute Runtime: 2 hours and 1 minute.
Source: Toronto Public Library — Young Adults

item.title: GO Train Hike - Unionville/Markham — Sun Sep 13, 9:00 AM
item.description:
Toronto Bruce Trail Club he villages of Unionville & Markham are connected by the Rouge Valley Trail System following the Rouge River and running behind the historic buildings on Main Street Unionville, by Walden Pond in Austin Drive Park, through Milne Dam Conservation Area, and ending with a 143 metre long suspension bridge over the dam. We will walk into the village of Markham and finish with a short boardwalk trail through Tannery Pond which is close to the Markham GO Station. We begin the hike at Unionville GO Station hiking north to the historic Main Street and picking up the Rouge Valley Trail at Carlton Road. Return to Toronto or the starting point by GO Train or York Region Transit bus. Optional stop at the Rouge River Craft Brewery after the hike. Terrain is easy, mostly paved path/boardwalk with some dirt trails. On The Go Maps Link: [https://onthegomap.com/s/g5rhpj1s](https://onthegomap.com/s/g5rhpj1s)
